concept.name: Holding period
concept.definition: The elapsed time between establishing and closing a position, defined consistently by timestamps or bars and summarized across trades or capital.
concept.intuition: It turns an informal trading idea into a claim or design choice that can be evaluated against dated evidence.
concept.mechanics: Record entry and exit timestamps for each lot, compute durations under a stated weighting convention, and relate them to forecast horizon and costs.
concept.formula: Holding period = exit timestamp - entry timestamp
concept.failure_modes: Results can mislead when hindsight, multiple testing, nonstationarity, costs, or unavailable historical information are ignored.
concept.misconceptions: A favorable historical result is evidence about the tested sample and assumptions, not proof of a durable profitable edge.
concept.example: A position opened Monday at 10:00 and closed Wednesday at 15:00 has a 53-hour calendar holding period.
